- the network allowlist field name and whether it accepts

name: driftmetrics-fleet-worker
description: DriftMetrics Acurast worker — claims a job from the Supabase queue, runs the siphon scan inside the TEE, posts the displacement report back, deletes the queue row.

schedule._comment: 30s × 30+ processors ≈ ~1 claim attempt per second across the fleet. Most return null (no work). claim_next_job uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so concurrent claims are safe.

requirements._comment: TEE has no persistent storage. siphon doesn't need any.

network._comment_egress: Only these hosts are reachable from inside the TEE. Adding a host requires re-deploying. The Supabase host is YOUR project URL — replace if you ever migrate.

secrets.name: SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY
secrets._comment: service_role JWT. Set via: acurast secrets set SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY <key>. Decrypted only inside the TEE; processor operator cannot read it.

_comment_selection: Three selection modes you'll see in Acurast docs (names may vary):
by_owner       — only your own processors (your wallet owns them).
This is what your 30+ Root Image fleet wants.
by_attestation — any processor with a verified TEE attestation.
by_device_ids  — explicit list of processor deviceIds. Most
restrictive. Use if you need to pin to a subset.

reward._comment: Owned-fleet jobs typically have zero reward — you're paying yourself. Set non-zero only if you want to incentivize external processors via 'by_attestation' selection.

consumers._comment: Even with zero reward, Acurast may require a consumer/funding address declared. Verify.
